newsitem.title: USA: Texaco aims to hike output 50 pct by 2001.
newsitem.headline: Texaco aims to hike output 50 pct by 2001.

text.p: Texaco Inc is planning to hike its worldwide oil production by fifty percent over the next five years to bring output to 1.7 million barrels of oil equivalent (BOE) per day by the year 2001.

At the company's annual analyst meeting at its headquaters, Chief Executive Officer Peter Bijur said U.S. production was projected to jump by 180,000 BOE a day, mostly from deepwater Gulf of Mexico operations. And North Sea output is set to increase by 108,000 BOE per day, he said.
Bijur said the company "needed to sustain production increases, which we consider our lifeblood."

He said the company aims to increase output in the U.S. Gulf, the North Sea, South America, Nigeria, Southeast Asia and China and Kazakstan, and the Partitioned Neutral Zone between Saudi Arabia and Kuwait.

North Sea production will be boosted by the Captain project, expected to come on line this month, and the Erskine project due to come onstream in October 1997, according to Robert Soldberg, president of Texaco's Middle East/Far East division.
